Browser Automation is the code-first way to build multi-step automations. The Skyvern SDK connects to a cloud Chromium instance over CDP, layers Playwright on top, and injects AI into every page interaction.
Build multi-step automations visually in the Cloud UI with drag-and-drop blocks. No code required. Share templates across your team.
The Skyvern MCP server lets AI assistants like Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Windsurf control a browser.
Skyvern handles logins with stored credentials, TOTP/authenticator codes, email and SMS verification, magic links, and password manager integrations with Bitwarden, 1Password, and Azure Key Vault.

Skyvern detects CAPTCHAs using its vision model and solves them automatically. This works for reCAPTCHA v2/v3, hCaptcha, Cloudflare Turnstile, FunCaptcha/ArkoseLabs, MTCaptcha, and standard text/number image CAPTCHAs.
Human-in-the-loop flows: pause for approval between steps without losing browser state. The VNC stream lets you watch or take control at any point.
Every run automatically captures what happened: recordings of the browser session, screenshots at each step, the AI's reasoning, and network traffic.
Self-hosted Skyvern runs entirely on your infrastructure: your servers, your browsers, your LLM API keys.
You're replacing brittle Selenium scripts, integrating browser automation via API, or building workflows into your product.
Auto-fill and submit applications on Lever, Greenhouse, and more.
Log into vendor portals, find invoices, download PDFs.

I tried it out and it's pretty pricey. My OpenAI API bill is $3.20 after using this on a few different pages to test it out... this is always going to be slower. What I'd love to see is a way to generate scrapers quickly.

I played with the Geico example, and it seems to do a good job on the happy path. But I tried costcotravel.com... it struggled to hit the 'rental car' tab... it entered JFK into the pickup location, but then failed to click the popup.
Exciting stuff, my employer would be interested but it's AGPL3 licensed so it's a non-starter for them.
I'm curious about the computer vision aspect of this tool... Definitely a step beyond existing browser automation software!
Unfortunately the mobile experience is pretty bad - practically unusable. I'd expect any web application made in the last decade to be mobile-first.
awesome work. I had the github starred from the day I saw on Show HN but never got around to using it. I want to use this to automate approving/declining group members for our facebook group.

you are expecting them to pass over their website login credentials and apparently their credit card details too, in plain text. You had better have a very solid idea of how to handle that sensitive data.

I can't see that option in Skyvern which would have me worrying that process changes would be overlooked and we would unknowingly start entering the wrong data or missing steps, unlike Playwright automations with assertions.

This is an impressive tool. I especially like the observability around the workflow and the steps it takes to achieve the outcome. We are potentially interested in exploring this if we can get the cost down at scale.
